# Get started with pubflow

{pipeflow} computes the results of an analysis in pipeline steps.
{pubflow} adds what you need to *publish* these results:

- **parameters** that describe themselves (label, limits, description)
  and check their values;
- **outputs** for documents: tables, figures and text;
- **documents** that steps of the pipeline build from these outputs;
- **reports** in HTML, Word and PDF format;
- **Shiny modules** for a parameter UI and a document viewer.

This vignette goes through all of them with one small example. It
assumes that you know how to build and run a pipeline; if not, read
pipeflow’s [Get
started](https://cran.r-project.org/package=pipeflow/vignettes/v01-get-started.html)
first.

### The example

We use the example of pipeflow’s Get started vignette: a pipeline that
adds a temperature column in degrees Celsius to base R’s `airquality`
data, fits a linear model of the ozone concentration and plots the fit.

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`pipeflow`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/)`)`\
\
`pip`` ``<-`` `[`pip_new`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_new.html)`(``"my-pip"``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"data"``, ``function``(``data`` ``=`` ``airquality``)`` ``data``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"prep"``, ``function``(``df`` ``=`` ``~``data``)`` ``{`\
`        ``df``[``, ``"Temp.Celsius"``]`` ``<-`` ``(``df``[``, ``"Temp"``]`` ``-`` ``32``)`` ``*`` ``5`` ``/`` ``9`\
`        ``df`\
`    ``}``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"fit"``, ``function``(``data`` ``=`` ``~``prep``, ``xVar`` ``=`` ``"Temp.Celsius"``)`` ``{`\
`        `[`lm`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html)`(`[`paste`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/paste.html)`(``"Ozone ~"``, ``xVar``)``, data ``=`` ``data``)`\
`    ``}``)`

To publish the results, we add three things: params that describe the
pipeline’s parameters, steps that turn the results into a table, a
figure and a text, and a step that arranges them into a document.

### Parameters

A pipeflow parameter is a plain R value, the default of a step
function’s argument. A pubflow parameter (a *param*) is a value with
attributes that describe it: a label, limits, a description, and so on.
A *param config* collects the params of an analysis:

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`pubflow`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/)`)`\
\
`config`` ``<-`` `[`param_config`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/param_config.md)`(`\
`    xVar ``=`` `[`choice_param`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/param.md)`(`\
`        ``"Temp.Celsius"``,`\
`        choices ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"Temp.Celsius"``, ``"Wind"``, ``"Solar.R"``)``,`\
`        label ``=`` ``"Predictor"``,`\
`        source ``=`` ``"user"``,`\
`        description ``=`` ``"Variable that explains the ozone concentration"`\
`    ``)``,`\
`    level ``=`` `[`numeric_param`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/param.md)`(`\
`        ``0.95``,`\
`        label ``=`` ``"Confidence level"``,`\
`        min ``=`` ``0.5``,`\
`        max ``=`` ``0.999``,`\
`        source ``=`` ``"user"`\
`    ``)``,`\
`    title ``=`` `[`param`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/param.md)`(`\
`        ``"Ozone in New York"``,`\
`        label ``=`` ``"Report title"``,`\
`        source ``=`` ``"user"`\
`    ``)`\
`)`\
`config`\
`# <param_config: 3 params>`\
`#  name  type      value                     label           `\
`#  xVar  factor    <factor[1]: Temp.Celsius> Predictor       `\
`#  level numeric   0.95                      Confidence level`\
`#  title character Ozone in New York         Report title`

Each kind of param checks its values:
[`choice_param()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/param.md)
allows only one of its `choices` (its value is a factor),
[`numeric_param()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/param.md)
only a number between `min` and `max`. `source = "user"` marks the
params that the user sets, so that an app or a report can pick them out.

### Outputs

The next steps turn the results into outputs that a document can show:
[`pub_table()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_table.md)
makes a table with column labels and the number of decimal places,
[`pub_figure()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_figure.md)
a figure with a caption, and
[`pub_text()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_text.md) a
text in Markdown.

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`ggplot2`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org)`)`\
\
`coef_table`` ``<-`` ``function``(``model``, ``level``)`` ``{`\
`    ``ci`` ``<-`` `[`confint`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/confint.html)`(``model``, level ``=`` ``level``)`\
`    ``coefs`` ``<-`` `[`data.frame`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/data.frame.html)`(`\
`        term ``=`` `[`rownames`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/colnames.html)`(``ci``)``,`\
`        estimate ``=`` `[`coef`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/coef.html)`(``model``)``,`\
`        lower ``=`` ``ci``[``, ``1L``]``,`\
`        upper ``=`` ``ci``[``, ``2L``]`\
`    ``)`\
`    `[`pub_table`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_table.md)`(`\
`        ``coefs``,`\
`        caption ``=`` `[`sprintf`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/sprintf.html)`(``"Coefficients with %g%% confidence limits"``, ``100`` ``*`` ``level``)``,`\
`        labels ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(`\
`            term ``=`` ``"Term"``,`\
`            estimate ``=`` ``"Estimate"``,`\
`            lower ``=`` ``"Lower"``,`\
`            upper ``=`` ``"Upper"`\
`        ``)``,`\
`        digits ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``estimate ``=`` ``3L``, lower ``=`` ``3L``, upper ``=`` ``3L``)`\
`    ``)`\
`}`\
\
`fit_figure`` ``<-`` ``function``(``model``, ``data``, ``xVar``)`` ``{`\
`    ``coefs`` ``<-`` `[`coef`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/coef.html)`(``model``)`\
`    ``p`` ``<-`` `[`ggplot`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggplot.html)`(``data``, `[`aes`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/aes.html)`(``.data``[[``xVar``]``]``, ``.data``$``Ozone``)``)`` ``+`\
`        `[`geom_point`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_point.html)`(``na.rm ``=`` ``TRUE``)`` ``+`\
`        `[`geom_abline`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_abline.html)`(``intercept ``=`` ``coefs``[[``1L``]``]``, slope ``=`` ``coefs``[[``2L``]``]``)`\
`    `[`pub_figure`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_figure.md)`(``p``, caption ``=`` ``"Linear model fit"``, width ``=`` ``6``, height ``=`` ``3.5``)`\
`}`

\
`pip`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"coef_table"``, ``function``(``model`` ``=`` ``~``fit``, ``level`` ``=`` ``0.95``)`` ``{`\
`        ``coef_table``(``model``, ``level``)`\
`    ``}``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"plot"``, ``function``(``model`` ``=`` ``~``fit``, ``data`` ``=`` ``~``prep``, ``xVar`` ``=`` ``"Temp.Celsius"``)`` ``{`\
`        ``fit_figure``(``model``, ``data``, `[`as.character`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/character.html)`(``xVar``)``)`\
`    ``}``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"summary"``, ``function``(``model`` ``=`` ``~``fit``)`` ``{`\
`        ``r2`` ``<-`` `[`summary`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html)`(``model``)``$``r.squared`\
`        `[`pub_text`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_text.md)`(`[`sprintf`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/sprintf.html)`(`\
`            ``"The model explains **%.0f%%** of the variance of the ozone concentration."``,`\
`            ``100`` ``*`` ``r2`\
`        ``)``)`\
`    ``}``)`

The table and the figure are made by functions defined outside the
pipeline (here `coef_table()` and `fit_figure()`). This matters for
figures: a ggplot keeps the environment it was made in, so a plot made
inside the pipeline’s code would keep the pipeline alive in every copy
of the figure.

### A document

The last step is a *layout step*: it takes the outputs of other steps
and arranges them into a document with
[`pub_doc()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md) and
[`pub_section()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md).

\
`pip`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(`\
`        ``"report"``,`\
`        ``function``(`\
`            ``title`` ``=`` ``""``,`\
`            ``summary`` ``=`` ``~``summary``,`\
`            ``table`` ``=`` ``~``coef_table``,`\
`            ``plot`` ``=`` ``~``plot`\
`        ``)`` ``{`\
`            `[`pub_doc`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(`\
`                `[`pub_section`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(``"Results"``, ``summary``, ``table``, ``plot``)``,`\
`                title ``=`` ``title`\
`            ``)`\
`        ``}`\
`    ``)`

Finally, we set the params of the config in the pipeline. Each param
goes to every step that has an argument of its name, here `xVar` to the
steps `fit` and `plot`:

\
[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``pip``, ``config``)`\
`pip`\
`# <pipeflow> my-pip (7 steps)`\
`# ---------------------------`\
`#          step                   params                 depends state`\
`# 1:       data                     data                           new`\
`# 2:       prep                       df                    data   new`\
`# 3:        fit                data,xVar                    prep   new`\
`# 4: coef_table              model,level                     fit   new`\
`# 5:       plot          model,data,xVar                fit,prep   new`\
`# 6:    summary                    model                     fit   new`\
`# 7:     report title,summary,table,plot summary,coef_table,plot   new`\
`# ---------------------------`\
`# <ready> last run: never`\
`# steps: 7 new`

The steps still get plain values: `coef_table` gets `level = 0.95`, not
the param object.
[`pub_get_params()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_get_params.md)
reads the params back from the pipeline:

\
[`names`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/names.html)`(`[`pub_get_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_get_params.md)`(``pip``)``)`\
`# [1] "xVar"  "level" "title"`

### Run and view

We run the pipeline and take the document from the output of the layout
step:

\
[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``pip``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)`\
`doc`` ``<-`` ``pip``[[``"report"``, ``"out"``]``]`\
`doc`\
`# <pubflow document> "Ozone in New York"`\
`# # Results`\
`#   text "The model explains **49%** of the var..."`\
`#   table "Coefficients with 95% confidence limits"`\
`#   figure "Linear model fit"`

[`pub_html()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_html.md)
renders the document to HTML. In an R Markdown document like this
vignette, the HTML is shown in place:

\
[`pub_html`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_html.md)`(``doc``)`

## Ozone in New York

- [1 Results](#pubflow-sec-1)

| Temp.Celsius |    4.372 |   3.540 |   5.203 |

### Change a param

Params are set with pipeflow’s
[`pip_set_params()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html).
pubflow checks the new value against the param’s rules before it is set:

\
[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``pip``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``xVar ``=`` ``"Solar.R"``)``)`\
[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``pip``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)`\
`pip``[[``"coef_table"``, ``"out"``]``]`

| Term        | Estimate | Lower |  Upper |
|-------------|---------:|------:|-------:|
| (Intercept) |   18.599 | 5.225 | 31.973 |
| Solar.R     |    0.127 | 0.062 |  0.192 |

Coefficients with 95% confidence limits {#tab:set-valid .table .huxtable
quarto-disable-processing="true"
style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;   break-inside: avoid; page-break-inside: avoid;"}

An invalid value is an error, and nothing is set:

\
[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``pip``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``xVar ``=`` ``"Height"``)``)`\
`# ``Error``:`\
`# ``!`` Cannot set 2 parameters: nothing was set.`\
`#   step 'fit', parameter 'xVar': value must be one of: Temp.Celsius, Wind, Solar.R`\
`#   step 'plot', parameter 'xVar': value must be one of: Temp.Celsius, Wind, Solar.R`\
[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``pip``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``level ``=`` ``1.5``)``)`\
`# ``Error``:`\
`# ``!`` Cannot set 1 parameter: nothing was set.`\
`#   step 'coef_table', parameter 'level': value must be less than or equal to max (0.999)`

### A report file

[`pub_render()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_render.md)
writes the document to a file with pandoc: a Word document, a PDF (via
LaTeX or Typst) or Markdown. The metadata given at render time appear in
the document, e.g. the author:

\
`file`` ``<-`` `[`pub_render`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_render.md)`(``doc``, ``"docx"``, meta ``=`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``author ``=`` ``"Jane Doe"``)``)`\
[`basename`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/basename.html)`(``file``)`\
`# [1] "20261107T182829Z_ozone_in_new_york.docx"`

By default, the file goes to R’s temporary directory, and its name is
made of the render time and the title. Word and PDF need pandoc (\>=
3.6); a PDF also needs a LaTeX installation (xelatex) or Typst (see the
[Reports
vignette](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/articles/v06-reports.md)):

\
[`pub_render`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_render.md)`(``doc``, ``"pdf"``, file ``=`` ``"ozone.pdf"``)`\
[`pub_render`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_render.md)`(``doc``, ``"pdf"``, file ``=`` ``"ozone.pdf"``, pdf_engine ``=`` ``"typst"``)`

[`pub_report_spec()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_report_spec.md)
sets up the format of a report: page size and margins, a title page, a
Word template, and more.

### A Shiny app

Two Shiny modules turn the pipeline into an app:
[`pub_params_ui()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_params_ui.md)
with
[`pub_pipeline_params_server()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_params_ui.md)
shows an input for every param of the pipeline and sets the values that
the user enters in the pipeline, and
[`pub_viewer_ui()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_viewer_ui.md)
with
[`pub_viewer_server()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_viewer_ui.md)
shows the document.

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`shiny`](https://shiny.posit.co/)`)`\
\
`ui`` ``<-`` `[`fluidPage`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/shiny/man/fluidPage.html)`(`\
`    `[`fluidRow`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/shiny/man/fluidPage.html)`(`\
`        `[`column`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/shiny/man/column.html)`(``4``, `[`pub_params_ui`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_params_ui.md)`(``"params"``)``)``,`\
`        `[`column`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/shiny/man/column.html)`(``8``, `[`pub_viewer_ui`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_viewer_ui.md)`(``"viewer"``, height ``=`` ``"90vh"``)``)`\
`    ``)`\
`)`\
\
`server`` ``<-`` ``function``(``input``, ``output``, ``session``)`` ``{`\
`    ``pip`` ``<-`` `[`pip_clone`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_clone.html)`(``pip``)`` ``# every session gets its own pipeline`\
`    ``params`` ``<-`` `[`pub_pipeline_params_server`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_params_ui.md)`(``"params"``, ``pip``)`\
`    ``doc`` ``<-`` `[`reactive`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/shiny/man/reactive.html)`(``{`\
`        ``params``$``revision``(``)`` ``# run again after every change of a param`\
`        `[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``pip``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)`\
`        ``pip``[[``"report"``, ``"out"``]``]`\
`    ``}``)`\
`    `[`pub_viewer_server`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_viewer_ui.md)`(``"viewer"``, ``doc``)`\
`}`\
\
[`shinyApp`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/shiny/man/shinyApp.html)`(``ui``, ``server``)`

An invalid input is marked and the last valid value is restored, so the
pipeline only ever gets valid values. A pipeline is a reference object,
so `server()` starts with a copy
([`pip_clone()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_clone.html)):
otherwise a change of a param in one session would also change the
pipeline of every other session.

The report app that comes with pubflow shows more: grouped params, two
reports from one pipeline, failed steps in the document and the download
of the report. Run it with

\
`shiny``::`[`runApp`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/shiny/man/runApp.html)`(`[`system.file`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/system.file.html)`(``"examples"``, ``"report-app"``, package ``=`` ``"pubflow"``)``)`

- params:

- outputs:
  [`?pub_table`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_table.md),

  [`?pub_text`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_text.md);
- documents:
  [`?pub_doc`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md),
  [`?pub_layout_inputs`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_layout_inputs.md);
- rendering and reports:
  [`?pub_html`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_html.md),
  [`?pub_render`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_render.md),
  [`?pub_report_spec`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_report_spec.md);
- Shiny:
